newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK leader-elect shaping his goverment and policy.
newsitem.headline: HK leader-elect shaping his goverment and policy.

text.p: Tung Chee-hwa, Hong Kong's leader-designate, has promised to seek dialogue with human rights groups often critical of China's record for upholding civil freedoms.

Tung, who was picked last week by a Beijing-supervised panel as the colony's chief executive when the territory reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997, spent the weekend making public appearances and dropping hints about the shape his government will take.
"I will meet all sorts of people, including the human rights people," Tung told reporters who trailed him on Saturday.
Tung said he will not be joining the Chinese Communist Party, despite having already made it clear he will legalise the party if he is asked to do so by China.
Until reforms introduced in 1990, all political parties were outlawed in Hong Kong by the British colonial authorities. The status of the Chinese Communist Party remains unclear.

Tung is expected to decide in coming weeks who will hold senior civil service positions and who will make up his advisory cabinet -- but not until after a trip to Beijing this week to accept his own appointment as Hong Kong's first Chief Executive.
"I would like to see the elite of society and those with a mission join me in the future," he said, adding he would admit people "from all classes" to his administration.
Tung has already said he would like Hong Kong's "iron lady," Anson Chan, the popular head of the civil service and deputy to colonial Governor Chris Patten, to stay.
Some analysts have speculated that senior officials who worked closely with Patten on his political reforms, which have infuriated Beijing, may not keep their jobs after the handover.
Taiwan was also on Tung's weekend agenda. He said he looked forward to maintaining relations between Hong Kong and the island that Beijing regards as a renegade province.
"(I hope to) continue to promote economic and cultural exchanges between Hong Kong and Taiwan," he said.

Tung, 59, is expected meet a number of senior Chinese leaders when he visits Beijing next week, including President Jiang Zemin. He is also expected to meet Premier Li Peng, and National People's Congress (parliament) chairman Qiao Shi.
